title: SR 44 over Mud Creek | 2018 rehabilitation design
source_note: INDOT B-38321, 34 sheets approved August 22, 2017. Models the 2018 rehabilitation design. Current inventory suffix B refers to later work; geometry here uses drawing suffix A.
assumptions: Reconstruction of the 2018 B-38321 rehabilitation design (drawings approved 2017-08-22), not a current-condition or as-built survey.
2026 B-44483 / 2200653 plans are supplementary evidence only; proposed deck-overlay work is not mixed into the 2018 geometric state.

Existing cap elevations and concrete dimensions are approximate in the primary drawings. The beam surfaces interpolate support/grade geometry; fabrication camber and construction screed allowances are excluded. Combining these approximate seat levels with the shim table yields some haunch gaps below the nominal 3/4-in minimum. These interfaces remain unresolved and require surveyed seat/beam levels; the model is therefore marked needs detail.

Original 1980 drawings supply retained wall ends, footing dimensions and design pile lengths. The 2017 drawings apply a -0.57-ft elevation adjustment. Actual driven pile tips are unknown; foundations are hidden by default.

Steel member root fillets and channel flange taper are omitted. Connection threads, washers, drilled holes, weld beads, internal pad laminations, shear studs embedded in concrete and internal reinforcement are not modeled.

Approach TGB steel guardrail, its terminal systems, drainage outlets, backfill, riprap/terrain and drip recesses remain outside the modeled scope. Wing and TFC transitions retain simplified envelope geometry.
Material colors are visualization choices and are not evidence of the actual coating or surface condition.
This GLB is not a validated FEM model. Joints, material calibration, loads and meshing require a separate engineering model.

detail_coverage.detail: All three spans, 46 ft 6 in width, 15-degree skew and 200-ft crest profile.
Seven continuous W27x94 lines in three fabrication segments; fourteen eight-plate splices with 104 bolts each. Loaded profile interpolated, fillets and holes omitted.

48 channel diaphragms in six regular and two skew support rows; connection plates and bolts. Regular rows: channels 1 in off the webs on 1/2 x 7 1/4 in plates, 16 bolts each. Pier rows: 5 ft 11 in channels on bent plates with 32 bolts each. Channel taper simplified.
28 pads, load plates and source shim stacks; side retainers at piers. Internal rubber laminations, washers and welds excluded.

Both wall piers and end bents. Stepped caps and wings are approximate existing envelopes, as stated on the plans; end-bent caps end at the wing faces with the 1980 front splays and square rear ends. Semi-integral end diaphragms with the 6 in pavement ledge, square to the roadway over the outer 1 ft 6 in at each coping.
Retained footings and 58 design piles from 1980 sheets 9/11. Unknown driven pile tips; hidden by default.
FC barriers, four TFC transitions, both skew-to-square approach slabs, four extensions and twelve schematic delineators.
TGB and terminal systems require additional standard details and exact station placement.
Existing drain outlets, riprap and ground geometry not reconstructed. Drip-bead recesses and east approach curbs not modeled.
No reinforcement cages, embedded shear studs, temporary detours or equipment.
